title: Where the step time goes: small op vs large op
caption: The dispatch overhead law at its two ends. A ~1 us elementwise kernel pays ~15 us of host issue cost for ~1 us of device work -- dispatch is ~94% of the step. A ~100 us GEMM pays the same fixed cost once, so dispatch drops to ~13%. The per-op cost is constant; only the denominator changes.

title: What you can write vs what the compiler can lower
caption: Operator counts mined from each project (latest snapshots in the book's data tables). Each bar is the eager API surface, split into the subset its compiler-facing set can lower versus the eager-only remainder: ~7% coverage for PyTorch, ~8% for TensorFlow, ~100% for JAX - lax is already the compiler's language. Export succeeds only inside the thin first segment.

title: ResNet-50 batch-64 training peak: activations are the mountain
caption: Book scenario ResNet50Fp32AdamBatch64, FP32. Weights are ~102 MB and Adam's two moments add ~204 MB -- together under 4% of the peak. Saved activations dominate: the low and high estimates bracket 8.4-12.4 GB total, 82-121x the weight storage. The batch knob scales only the activation slice.
